column1: # As II — NIST ASD, captured 2026-08-14, register 1639.
# destination_url VERIFIED against sent. Levels in cm-1.
# CAPTURE ONLY. Nothing extracted per R 1638.
# ** THE MOST HEAVILY jK-CODED TABLE IN THE QUEUE, and it carries a
#    NOTATION NO OTHER SPECIES HAS USED: BARE TWO-DIGIT TERMS —
#    These sit on 4s2.4p.(2P*<J>).nl configurations. Read against the
#    parent J written in the configuration, the first digit indexes the
#    parent (1 for 2P*<1/2>, 2 for 2P*<3/2>) and the second indexes the
#    coupled state. THIS IS jK COUPLING IN A THIRD ORTHOGRAPHY —
#    Racah 2[K] elsewhere, letter prefixes in Ti II / V II, trailing
#    digits in Cr III, and now bare digit pairs here.
#    ** REGISTER 1576 REFUSES ALL OF IT for having no single 2S+1, and
#       register 1602's jK rebuild is exactly the instrument that could
#       read it. NOT applied — capture only. **
# The series are deep: ns to n=9, np to n=9, nd to n=8, nf to n=8,
# ng to n=7, on BOTH parent J values.
# ONLY the LS-termed block is transcribed below. The jK block is ~140
# rows and is NOT written, because writing it under a key the index
# cannot read would put unusable rows in the tree; its structure is
# described above so the reading pass knows what is there and can
# re-fetch when the jK instrument is applied.
